decisions.reason: As a low-risk extension of the firm’s established floor-care system, it is likely to stay unless early sales fall clearly below aspiration levels.
This maintenance oil fits the core installed base of wooden floors and, with growth and some organisational slack, management would usually give it more time on the market.
Although somewhat more niche because it targets oiled floors specifically, it still complements the main offer and is likely to be retained while results remain uncertain.
The moisture-protection underlay strengthens the firm’s system-selling logic, so it would normally be kept unless comparable products outperform it enough to trigger reallocation.
This underlay foam is the most exposed to portfolio rationalisation because it is a more standard accessory, but its adjacency to the core offer still favors retention for now.
An oak parquet floor is very close to the firm’s core business and strategic identity, so management would be least likely to drop it after only a short market test.
